title: MID: Mask-Image Distributional Divergence for Evaluating Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2610.17354v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Current evaluation protocols for medical image segmentation remain largely anchored in sample-wise comparisons, e.g., Dice and Hausdorff distance, which require each prediction to be paired with a ground-truth mask. Yet two limitations arise in practice: they are inapplicable when predictions are made on unlabeled data; and even when annotations are available, they cannot assess whether a collection of predictions matches the distributional structure of the ground-truth population. We introduce MID (Mask-Image Distributional Divergence), a distribution-level evaluation metric for medical image segmentation. MID builds upon the observation that segmentation quality is a property of the joint image-mask distribution: a mask may be anatomically plausible in isolation yet incorrect for the image it accompanies. MID compares the joint distribution of images and masks between a reference set and a set of predictions, without requiring sample

translated_title: MID：用于医学图像分割评估的掩码-图像分布散度
translated_abstract: 当前医学图像分割的评估协议仍主要依赖于样本级别的比较，例如Dice系数和Hausdorff距离，这些方法要求每个预测必须与真实标注掩码配对。然而在实践中存在两个局限：当在无标注数据上进行预测时，这些方法无法适用；即使标注可用，它们也无法评估一组预测是否匹配真实数据总体的分布结构。我们提出了MID（掩码-图像分布散度），这是一种分布级的医学图像分割评估指标。MID基于这样一个观察：分割质量是图像-掩码联合分布的一种属性——一个掩码在孤立来看可能在解剖学上是合理的，但相对于它所伴随的图像而言却是错误的。MID通过比较参考集与预测集之间图像和掩码的联合分布来进行评估，无需样本……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出MID（掩码-图像分布散度），一种分布级医学图像分割评估指标，通过比较参考集与预测集的图像-掩码联合分布，摆脱对样本级配对标注的依赖，并能评估预测集合是否匹配真实数据的分布结构。
en_tdlr: MID (Mask-Image Distributional Divergence) is a distribution-level evaluation metric for medical image segmentation that compares the joint image-mask distribution between a reference set and predictions, removing the need for sample-wise ground-truth pairing and assessing whether predictions match the distributional structure of the ground-truth population.
